text:
maria (support): FYI received an escalation from a customer (ClipperAI) after last night's rollout. They say long conversations start losing the original system instructions and early messages are effectively ignored after ~20k tokens. They provided a repro curl and say previous model behavior was fine. No 500s, but quality regression.

simon (cs): got it — they attached a minimal repro and a session transcript. Do we know which model variant rolled out?

maria (support): rollout note says model=v2.4-optimized, kernel changes to 'continuous-batching' enabled. customer says latency is slightly higher too (median -> 650ms from ~420ms). No auth/billing issues.

josh (eng-research): Thanks. Can you paste the exact curl + headers + token counts? Also does the transcript show any truncation indicators from our side?

maria (support): pasted from customer (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer" 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
 -d '{"model":"v2.4-optimized","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant that always asks for clarifying questions."}, {"role":"user","content":"Step 1: ... (very long) ... Step N: final prompt"}], "max_tokens":512, "stream":false}'
```
They sent token counts from client: total input tokens ~21000 before generation, response tokens ~480. They said older model v2.3 kept system prompt behavior.

lisa (ml-eng): Interesting. No 500s suggests not an auth/ingest problem. Two hypotheses: (1) KV cache eviction/prefix trimming due to new batching/kernel behavior causing early context to be dropped, (2) different tokenizer/offset behaviour in v2.4-optimized leading to tokenization shifts so system prompt is effectively shifted out of the retained window.

maria (support): Customer also reports occasional 'truncated' markers in their client logs (they added a screenshot) but our API logs don't show errors.

josh (eng-research): @deploy-bot can you confirm which flags were toggled in last night's canary?

deploy-bot: Canary deploy completed 1947580000. Flags: continuous_batching=on, prefix_cache_eviction_threshold=0.6 -> 0.45 (experiment), kernel_set=fast-attn-v3.

lisa (ml-eng): That prefix_cache_eviction_threshold drop stands out. If eviction becomes more aggressive we could be evicting early KV entries under long sessions. Ask customer for an exact timestamp + request-id so we can check routing and cache metrics.

maria (support): Asked for x-request-id. They replied: x-request-id: c-9a7f2b3e, timestamp 2026-03-16T23:12:41Z. Repro request included in thread.

josh (eng-research): Pulling logs now.

opsbot: Trace c-9a7f2b3e: routed to pool-dedicated-12, model v2.4-optimized, node gpu-rt-07. Latency 712ms, tokens consumed by step: 21020 input / 480 output. Cache hit rate for session: 12%.

lisa (ml-eng): Cache hit rate 12% is alarmingly low for a long-running session. That supports eviction hypothesis. Do we have per-request eviction events?

josh (eng-research): Found multiple cache-eviction logs around that session: 
```
[2026-03-16T23:12:36Z] evict_prefix session=clipper-abc, threshold=0.45, evicted_prefix_bytes=28764
[2026-03-16T23:12:38Z] evict_prefix session=clipper-abc, threshold=0.45, evicted_prefix_bytes=16384
```
Looks like early tokens were evicted right before generation.

maria (support): Customer said behavior started immediately after rollout. They asked for a hotfix or rollback.

simon (cs): Customer is P0 for us — their production app is failing. They need a mitigation. Can we provide a temporary config they can set client-side?

lisa (ml-eng): Short-term mitigation options: 1) Pin to v2.3 (previous model) — requires us to allow old model variant for them (support can enable). 2) Increase prefix retention via request-level header: X-Session-Cache: preserve_full_prefix (we can short-circuit eviction for whitelisted sessions) — we can toggle per-customer but needs eng-infra change. 3) Ask them to send the system prompt as both system and repeated user message at the end of history (hacky).

maria (support): I'll offer pinning to v2.3 and the repeat-system prompt workaround for immediate relief. Opening an internal incident to track product fix.

josh (eng-research): Root cause plan: revert prefix_cache_eviction_threshold to prior value (0.6) for canary immediately, run a quick canary rollback, and run repro at scale. If that resolves, schedule a safer tuning rollout with longer TTL and additional cache telemetry.

deploy-bot: Rolling flag change: prefix_cache_eviction_threshold -> 0.6 (target: canary cluster). Started at 1947654500.

opsbot: Flag change applied to pool-dedicated-12 at 1947654600.

maria (support): Customer confirmed on quick test: system prompt behavior restored on pinned v2.3 and also appears fixed after flag reversion. They pushed a minor update and say latency back to ~430ms.

simon (cs): Good. We've offered to keep them on v2.3 for 48 hours while we validate the tuned v2.4. They accepted.

lisa (ml-eng): Action items: (1) create regression test using long-session transcripts (>=20k input tokens) against new kernels and batching settings, (2) add eviction telemetry to session-level traces (count evictions, evicted_bytes), (3) add a safety gate that prevents eviction during request processing while generation is in-flight. I'll file PRs.

josh (eng-research): Also add a short-term alert when cache_hit_rate < 25% for long-sessions.

maria (support): Marking this P1 incident. Escalated to eng-ml and eng-infra. Notifying customer success to coordinate.

simon (cs): I'll follow up with ClipperAI and confirm timeline. :thumbsup:

maria (support): Thanks everyone. Keeping thread open for final postmortem notes.

lisa (ml-eng): will draft postmortem after we merge fixes and validate.

josh (eng-research): Logging final notes: likely culprit = aggressive prefix eviction introduced as experiment; mitigation = revert threshold + per-customer pin.

maria (support): Closing loop with customer in 2h with summary and next steps.
